mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic activity, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 10% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in 5 days.
failure_condition: If unemployment rises above 10% but S&P 500 returns remain positive.

mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rate coupled with high unemployment indicates economic stress, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If both FEDFUNDS is low and UNRATE is high but S&P 500 returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in industrial production during an expansion signals strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: If industrial production grows but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment indicates a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 5 days.
failure_condition: If payroll employment increases but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in retail sales signals strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: If retail sales increase significantly but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: High GDP growth with high federal funds rate indicates inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is high and FEDFUNDS is high but S&P 500 returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in federal funds rate above 2% indicates monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS rises above 2% but S&P 500 returns are positive.
